metadata.title: AI Reliability Theory Foundations — Sources
metadata.description: Primary texts, standards, and references for 11 reliability theory primitives: MTBF/MTTR, availability composition, hazard functions, bathtub curve, fault tree analysis, FMEA, redundancy math, error budgets, Weibull analysis, system reliability, reliability allocation.
metadata.chapter_citation_note: Chapter-level citations for Lewis (1995), O'Connor & Kleyner (2012), and Birolini (2017) were removed 2026-07-11. A July-2026 audit found the per-primitive chapter numbers could not be verified against the books' actual tables of contents (spot-checked against a confirmed 2nd-ed. Lewis ToC) and, for Birolini, the same 'Chapter 2' was attributed to seven unrelated primitives — a strong fabrication signal. These sources remain valid topical references; cite them at the book level, not the chapter level, until someone verifies chapter numbers against a physical copy of each edition.

books.name: Introduction to Reliability Engineering (2nd ed.)
books.author: Lewis, E. E.
books.description: Foundational reliability engineering textbook covering MTBF/MTTR, availability and composition, hazard functions, the bathtub curve, fault tree analysis, system reliability, and reliability allocation. Chapter-level attributions previously listed here were not verified and have been removed (see chapter_citation_note above) — cite at the book level.

books.name: Practical Reliability Engineering (5th ed.)
books.author: O'Connor, P. D. T., & Kleyner, A.
books.description: Comprehensive practitioner reference covering MTBF/MTTR, availability, hazard functions, the bathtub curve, FMEA, FTA, redundancy, Weibull analysis, system reliability, and allocation. Strongly recommended for worked examples and test planning. Chapter-level attributions previously listed here were not verified and have been removed (see chapter_citation_note above) — cite at the book level.

books.name: Reliability Engineering: Theory and Practice (8th ed.)
books.author: Birolini, A.
books.description: Rigorous treatment of reliability theory with stochastic process foundations: hazard functions, availability and Markov models, FTA and FMEA, redundancy math, Weibull analysis, system reliability with common-cause failures, and allocation. Chapter-level attributions previously listed here (repeated 'ch. 2' across seven unrelated primitives) were a fabrication signal and have been removed (see chapter_citation_note above) — cite at the book level.

books.name: Site Reliability Engineering
books.author: Beyer, B., Jones, C., Petoff, J., & Murphy, N. R.
books.description: Google SRE book. Primary source for error budget concept (ch. 3–4), SLO design, availability measurement, and error-budget governance. Free online at sre.google.

books.name: The Site Reliability Workbook
books.author: Beyer, B., Murphy, N. R., Rensin, D. K., Kawahara, K., & Thorne, S.
books.description: Google SRE Workbook. Primary source for multi-window, multi-burn-rate alerting (ch. 5, 'Alerting on SLOs'), SLO implementation (ch. 2), and alerting thresholds. Free online at sre.google. (Chapter numbers verified against the published table of contents 2026-07-11.)

papers_and_standards.name: A statistical distribution function of wide applicability
papers_and_standards.author: Weibull, W.
papers_and_standards.description: Original paper introducing the Weibull distribution. Foundational source for primitive 09 (Weibull analysis) and the shape-parameter formulation used in primitives 03 and 04.

papers_and_standards.name: IEEE Std 1413-2010: Methodology for Reliability Prediction and Assessment for Electronic Systems and Equipment
papers_and_standards.author: IEEE
papers_and_standards.description: IEEE standard for reliability prediction methodology. Source for AGREE allocation method, prediction process, and failure-rate data requirements. Cited in primitives 01, 07, 10, 11.

papers_and_standards.name: IEC 60812:2018 — Failure modes and effects analysis (FMEA and FMECA)
papers_and_standards.author: IEC
papers_and_standards.description: International standard for FMEA process, worksheet structure, RPN scoring, and FMECA criticality analysis. Primary normative reference for primitive 06.

papers_and_standards.name: IEC 61025:2006 — Fault tree analysis (FTA)
papers_and_standards.author: IEC
papers_and_standards.description: International standard for FTA methodology, gate definitions, minimal cut set computation (MOCUS), and importance measures. Primary normative reference for primitive 05.

papers_and_standards.name: IEC 61508-6:2010 — Functional safety: Guidelines on IEC 61508-2 and -3
papers_and_standards.author: IEC
papers_and_standards.description: Part 6 provides guidance on common-cause failure (CCF) beta-factor quantification and systematic capability assessment for safety instrumented systems. Source for beta-factor common-cause model in primitive 10.

papers_and_standards.name: MIL-HDBK-217F — Reliability Prediction of Electronic Equipment
papers_and_standards.author: US Department of Defense
papers_and_standards.description: US DoD handbook for electronic component failure rate prediction. Widely cited but known to overstate failure rates for modern components. Use field data in preference to MIL-HDBK-217 predictions where available. Cited with caveat in primitives 04 and indirectly in 10.
papers_and_standards.caveat: Field data from MIL-HDBK-217 should be validated against observed rates; known to overstate failure rates in modern semiconductor and COTS components.

papers_and_standards.name: NIST/SEMATECH Engineering Statistics Handbook Chapter 8: Reliability
papers_and_standards.author: NIST/SEMATECH
papers_and_standards.description: NIST engineering statistics reference for reliability terms, acceleration, censoring, failure rate, lifetime distribution models, repair rate, and survival functions. Use for statistical reliability claims and lifetime-distribution checks.

papers_and_standards.name: Fault Tree Handbook (NUREG-0492)
papers_and_standards.author: US Nuclear Regulatory Commission
papers_and_standards.description: Official NRC fault-tree handbook. Source for fault tree construction, evaluation, gates, event trees, and system safety/reliability course material. Use as an accessible public reference for primitive 05.

papers_and_standards.name: Nonparametric estimation from incomplete observations
papers_and_standards.author: Kaplan, E. L., & Meier, P.
papers_and_standards.journal: Journal of the American Statistical Association
papers_and_standards.description: Foundational paper for the Kaplan-Meier estimator. Used for empirical survival/reliability estimation with right-censored data — the non-parametric baseline before fitting a Weibull model (primitive 09) or estimating hazard functions (primitive 03).

papers_and_standards.name: Reliability Engineering and Risk Analysis: A Practical Guide (3rd ed.)
papers_and_standards.author: Modarres, M., Kaminskiy, M. P., & Krivtsov, V.
papers_and_standards.description: Comprehensive treatment of probability distributions for reliability, Bayesian reliability methods, common-cause failures, and system reliability with imperfect maintenance. Complements Lewis and O'Connor for advanced applications. Corrected 2026-07-11: previously misfiled under id 'Bourne2021' with an unverifiable '4th ed. 2021' / ISBN 978-0-367-48700-8 combination that resolves to the 3rd edition (2017), not a 4th edition — no 4th edition of this title was found to exist as of 2026-07-11.

papers_and_standards.name: Software Reliability Modelling
papers_and_standards.author: Xie, M.
papers_and_standards.description: Software reliability growth models: Jelinski-Moranda, NHPP-based models (Goel-Okumoto, Musa-Okumoto). Relevant when applying reliability primitives to software systems where failure rate decreases as bugs are fixed — a DFR analogue for software.

papers_and_standards.name: An Empirical Study of Production Incidents in Generative AI Cloud Services
papers_and_standards.author: Yan, H., Chen, Y., Ma, M., Wen, M., Lu, S., Zhang, S., Xu, T., et al.
papers_and_standards.venue: ISSRE 2025 — 36th IEEE International Symposium on Software Reliability Engineering
papers_and_standards.description: Empirical analysis of 4 years of GenAI cloud service incidents (Microsoft). Key finding: GenAI incidents take 1.83× longer to mitigate vs. non-GenAI; monitor false-alarm rate 11.0% vs. 3.8%; root causes: infrastructure 27.2%, configuration 24.5%, code bugs 21.5%. Failure modes and mitigation strategies differ materially from traditional cloud services. Impacts MTBF/MTTR calibration (primitive 01) and error-budget thresholds (primitive 08).

papers_and_standards.name: ReliabilityBench: Evaluating LLM Agent Reliability Under Production-Like Stress Conditions
papers_and_standards.author: Gupta, A.
papers_and_standards.description: Benchmark evaluating LLM agent reliability across three dimensions: consistency (pass^k), robustness to perturbations (ε), and fault tolerance under API failures (λ). Key finding: perturbations reduce success from 96.9% to 88.1% at ε=0.2; rate limiting is the most damaging fault. ReAct more fault-tolerant than Reflexion. Single-run success rate is a misleading reliability metric. 1,280 episodes across 4 domains, 2 LLMs, 2 architectures.

papers_and_standards.name: Efficient Evaluation of LLM Performance with Statistical Guarantees
papers_and_standards.author: Wu, S., Nair, Y., & Candès, E. J.
papers_and_standards.description: Factorized Active Querying (FAQ): adaptive benchmark evaluation that delivers up to 5× effective sample size gains over uniform sampling while maintaining valid frequentist CI coverage. Frames LLM evaluation as finite-population inference; uses Bayesian factor model for historical leverage and active-learning for question selection. Directly relevant to reducing sample-size requirements in reliability estimation from AI system observations.

papers_and_standards.name: Chaos Engineering: A Multi-Vocal Literature Review
papers_and_standards.author: Owotogbe, J., Kumara, I., Van Den Heuvel, W.-J., & Tamburri, D. A.
papers_and_standards.description: Multivocal literature review of 96 chaos engineering sources (2016–2024). Derives unified definition of chaos engineering as a resilience testing practice using controlled fault injection. Builds taxonomy of chaos engineering platforms. Critically identifies lack of standardized quantitative metrics (MTTR/MTTD) as open research gap. Chaos engineering serves as empirical validation of redundancy coverage assumptions (primitive 07) and switchover reliability.

papers_and_standards.name: AI-driven FMEA: integration of large language models for faster and more accurate risk analysis
papers_and_standards.author: El Hassani, I., Masrour, T., Kourouma, N., & Tavčar, J.
papers_and_standards.description: LLM-augmented FMEA framework using GPT-4, GPT-4o, and Gemini to automate failure mode identification from unstructured field data. GPT-4 achieves 91% substantial agreement with expert gold standard on 100 reviews; part ID accuracy 98-99%. Prompt engineering in 2-3 iterations sufficient. Human-in-the-loop validation remains essential. Impacts primitive 06 (FMEA) tooling.

papers_and_standards.name: Towards a Science of AI Agent Reliability
papers_and_standards.author: Rabanser, S., Kapoor, S., Kirgis, P., Liu, K., Utpala, S., & Narayanan, A.
papers_and_standards.description: Proposes 12 concrete metrics decomposing AI agent reliability across four dimensions: consistency, robustness, predictability, and safety. Argues single-run success metrics obscure critical operational flaws — agents may succeed on average but fail consistently under perturbation or repeated execution. Directly extends system reliability primitives (01, 10) into the AI agent domain. Dashboard (hal.cs.princeton.edu/reliability, Princeton) confirmed live, evaluates 15 agents across 2 benchmarks on 12 metrics as of 2026-07-11.
papers_and_standards.verified_via: WebFetch 2026-05-17; re-verified WebFetch 2026-07-11 (venue update to ICML 2026, dashboard content confirmed)

papers_and_standards.name: Beyond pass@1: A Reliability Science Framework for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
papers_and_standards.author: Khanal, A., Tao, Y., & Zhou, J.
papers_and_standards.description: Introduces four reliability metrics for long-horizon agents: RDC (Reliability Decay Curve) — pass@1 degradation as task duration grows; VAF (Variance Amplification Factor) — how duration amplifies stochastic variance; GDS (Graceful Degradation Score) — performance decline continuity; MOP (Meltdown Onset Point) — behavioral collapse detection. Empirical study: 396 tasks, 23,392 episodes, 10 models. Key finding: capability and reliability rankings diverge substantially at long horizons; frontier models exhibit unexpectedly high failure rates. Code availability: not confirmed public as of 2026-05-17.

papers_and_standards.name: Measuring the Unmeasurable: Markov Chain Reliability for LLM Agents
papers_and_standards.author: Tran-Truong, P. T., & Le, X.-B.
papers_and_standards.description: Proposes TraceToChain: fits agent execution traces to absorbing Markov chains using Laplace-smoothed MLE, AIC+KS goodness-of-fit, and Dirichlet-posterior credible intervals. Demonstrates that pass@k, pass^k, and RDC are projections of one success-time distribution. Validated across seven agent frameworks; max L∞ error 0.053. Enables composition of per-step reliabilities for sequential tool-call chains — a direct extension of primitive 10 (system reliability). Code availability: not confirmed public as of 2026-05-17.

papers_and_standards.name: Engineering a Safer World: Systems Thinking Applied to Safety
papers_and_standards.author: Leveson, N. G.
papers_and_standards.description: Foundational monograph introducing STAMP (System-Theoretic Accident Model and Processes) and STPA (System-Theoretic Process Analysis). Models accidents as control-loop failures rather than component-chain failures, enabling analysis of software errors, design flaws, and human-automation coupling hazards invisible to FTA Boolean gate analysis. Cited 3,000+; adopted by FAA, FDA, and autonomous vehicle programs. Free PDF historically available via MIT STAMP project (sunnyday.mit.edu). Primary source for STPA callout in primitive 05.
papers_and_standards.verified_via: Canonical MIT Press title confirmed; sunnyday.mit.edu connection refused 2026-05-17 (known transient issue — book and free PDF are well-established)

papers_and_standards.name: Safety-I and Safety-II: The Past and Future of Safety Management
papers_and_standards.author: Hollnagel, E.
papers_and_standards.description: Introduces Safety-II: the perspective that reliability and safety emerge from understanding adaptive capacity (what normally goes right), not only enumerating failures (what goes wrong). Proposes FRAM (Functional Resonance Analysis Method) to model how work functions couple and resonate. Influential in SRE/resilience engineering communities (Hochstein, Allspaw). Complements FTA/FMEA as Safety-I methods. See also Ham 2020 (PMC7940128) for concise introduction.
papers_and_standards.verified_via: FRAM site (functionalresonance.com) confirmed Hollnagel authorship; Ham 2020 PMC7940128 verified via WebFetch 2026-05-17

papers_and_standards.name: Safety-II and Resilience Engineering in a Nutshell: An Introductory Guide to Their Concepts and Methods
papers_and_standards.author: Ham, D.-H.
papers_and_standards.description: Accessible peer-reviewed introduction to Safety-II and resilience engineering. Key claim: 'successful and failed work performance have the same causes' — variability in worker performance is normal, not deviant, and is the foundation of both safe and unsafe outcomes in sociotechnical systems. Use as entry point before Hollnagel 2014.
papers_and_standards.verified_via: WebFetch 2026-05-17 — title, author, journal, year, PMC ID confirmed
